question:
What is the degree measure of the smaller angle formed by the hands of a clock at \(10\) o’clock?

[Figure 1](figures/1999_AMC_8_Q02_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
At \(10\) o'clock, the hour hand points to \(10\) and the minute hand points to \(12\). The twelve equal hour intervals divide a full \(360^\circ\) turn, so each interval measures
\[
360^\circ\div12=30^\circ.
\]
The shorter way from \(10\) to \(12\) passes through \(11\), spanning two intervals. Thus the smaller angle is \(2\cdot30^\circ=\boxed{60^\circ}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
